items.title: [ChatGPT Work / Scheduled][Connectors] Multi-provider write failures in unattended runs; manual execution usually works (Sep–Oct 2026)

labels.name: safety-check
labels.description: Issues related to safety and abuse checks

items.body:
## Summary

Since approximately mid/late September 2026, a fleet of recurring **ChatGPT Work / Scheduled Tasks on the web** has suffered intermittent connector failures that are strongly **execution-surface dependent**. The owner reports that **manually initiated / interactive workflows generally work with the same connected services**, while unattended scheduled runs intermittently complete research or reads but cannot persist their results. In some cases a small, already-authorized GitHub mutation is stopped by **OpenAI's safety checks before GitHub can respond**; other cases involve different Google Drive/Docs tool/runtime defects.

This affects **multiple connector families, not just GitHub**. The first-hand evidence in this report is specifically **GitHub and Google Drive/Docs**. We do **not** claim every connector has been individually tested or that they all fail with the same error. Independent reports describe comparable scheduled-write authorization symptoms in Gmail, Google Sheets, and Trello (linked below).

**Important scope:** This is about the hosted **ChatGPT Work scheduled/automation execution path**, *not a locally reproduced bug in the open-source Codex CLI or Windows sandbox*. This repository already tracks related ChatGPT Web/automations issues (#48940 and #38350); please route to the owning runtime/connectors team if a different tracker is canonical.

## Environment and scope

- Product: ChatGPT Web / Work; recurring unattended Scheduled Tasks, with separately invoked manual / interactive runs for comparison.
- Operational pattern: approximately **15 enabled hourly agents** across independent projects during the 2026-10-10 investigation. Their recorded last-run timestamps showed invocation, **not** that work completed or was persisted.
- Connected apps investigated: **GitHub** and **Google Drive / native Google Docs**.
- Permission configuration independently checked by the owner: **Allow all actions** for **each** of GitHub and Google Drive. A lower global default for other apps does not override those app-specific settings.
- Repository access and interactive connector writes work in at least some owner-triggered executions (including creation and readback of the public diagnostic issue linked below).
- Exact model, reasoning effort, task-run trace IDs, internal policy decisions and connector/backend builds **are not visible** through the accessible Scheduled-task inspector. There is **no completed controlled model A/B comparison**. We cannot attribute this to “large models” or a particular Codex version.
- Failure is intermittent; neither a successful manual write nor a healthy single scheduled run establishes a permanent fix.

## What actually fails (keep these failure layers separate)

### A. GitHub: authorized writes refused while reads/other writes succeed

Some scheduled jobs can inspect repositories or otherwise run normally but fail to persist by `create_blob`, `create_file`, or `update_file`. Recorded operator/worker reports include the tool-facing message:

```
This tool call was blocked by OpenAI's safety checks.
```

A particularly useful history:
- A scheduled workflow's GitHub `create_blob` operation was blocked, while later work on the same code/repository path succeeded (see [EndlessZen #250, Oct 8 evidence](https://github.com/drevendev/EndlessZen/issues/250#issuecomment-6068892583)).
- A scheduled worker reported `create_file` rejected even though owner-session/interactive GitHub writes had succeeded ([EndlessZen #249, Oct 8 evidence](https://github.com/drevendev/EndlessZen/issues/249#issuecomment-6068830628)).
- This interactive session successfully **created and read back** the related owner-authored investigation issue [EndlessZen #260](https://github.com/drevendev/EndlessZen/issues/260). That verifies a working interactive GitHub write path on Oct 10; it is **not** proof of a byte-identical scheduled-vs-manual test, which remains needed.

A host-side safety refusal is **not** a GitHub HTTP 403, expired OAuth token, or a provider rejection unless the provider was actually called and such a response was captured. For many failures that distinction is invisible to the operator.

### B. Drive/Docs: a different set of failure boundaries

- Google Drive file upload workflows encountered an apparent missing **runtime file-reference / file handoff** even in a non-ledger diagnostic, so the run could not complete an upload ([EndlessZen #250, evidence](https://github.com/drevendev/EndlessZen/issues/250#issuecomment-6023744193)). This is not automatically a Google OAuth failure.
- Native Google Docs positional insertion sometimes **returned success but damaged adjacent text** (e.g. isolated `0` or malformed `+03:000` clock field) when the client guessed a structural insertion index, even with a revision guard ([EndlessZen #250, evidence](https://github.com/drevendev/EndlessZen/issues/250#issuecomment-6023680917)). This is a **corrupt-success / insertion-contract** failure, not proof that the same safety layer caused it.
- Both types prevent reliable persistence and recovery, even if the model's analysis or a prior read succeeds.

### C. Failure amplification and loss of diagnostics

One denied or ambiguous persistence step can make later hourly runs look like “no work”, freeze local agent progress accounting, or cause duplicate writes when the worker guesses whether the previous call took effect. That local accounting deadlock is also an application design defect and **should not be blamed entirely on OpenAI**; our own mitigation is being tracked separately in [EndlessZen #249/#250](https://github.com/drevendev/EndlessZen/issues/260).

Crucially, **a worker whose GitHub/Drive writes are blocked cannot be required to save its own error log to those same systems**. When a tool call is refused before provider dispatch, the model may receive only the generic refusal, not the underlying policy decision or request ID. If the run also fails before returning a result, the operator has no raw error to attach.

## Scheduled vs manual comparison (current strength of evidence)

| Context | Observed outcome | Limitation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unattended hourly Work/Scheduled runs | Intermittent refusal at GitHub write or Drive/Docs persistence despite enabled jobs and per-app Allow all actions | Not every run fails; different error classes exist |
| Owner-initiated / interactive workflows | Owner reports normal operation in ordinary manual execution; interactive GitHub issue creation/readback was independently verified | This is **not** yet a controlled identical-payload A/B across all providers |
| Missing run/connector data | A failed external write may leave no durable report and sometimes no exposed low-level error | Absence of a GitHub commit is not itself proof of any particular safety, network, auth or policy layer |

Independent issue [#48940](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/48940) and its comments contain **stronger exact-payload interactive-vs-scheduled reproductions** for GitHub, including a scheduled `create_file` safety refusal followed by successful interactive creation of the actual previously blocked article payload.

## Suggested reproducible test for OpenAI

1. In a test ChatGPT account, connect GitHub and Google Drive, set **Allow all actions** for both, and choose disposable test destinations with explicit authorization. Verify the current owner/target; do not test with real private content.
2. Create a minimal recurring **Scheduled Task** that first reads and then writes one small deterministic GitHub fixture under a fixed path, followed by readback. A separate scheduled task should create/update a small Drive/Docs fixture with exact readback. Do not depend on one tool to store the other tool's diagnostic.
3. Use the same connector account and **same safe fixture payload** in a manually started workflow. Test scheduled vs manually initiated run explicitly (and ordinary interactive, if these are different surfaces) while controlling for prompt, model when visible, task version, time and file size.
4. Repeat over enough scheduled intervals to catch intermittent outcomes. Preserve a host-owned per-run trace with execution context, tool action, gate type, whether provider dispatch occurred, redacted provider response/request ID, timing, approval state and verified external after-state.
5. Test independent failure classes separately: a refused GitHub mutation, missing upload handoff, and a syntactically successful but semantically corrupted Docs mutation. Do not treat all as “the connector disconnected.”

**Expected:** An authorized, supported connector action should behave consistently between manual and scheduled contexts, or clearly explain a documented policy/scope difference before dispatch. Unattended jobs should never be left indistinguishably “successful” when the requested remote effect did not occur. Generic “safety checks” denials need a concrete, supported remediation/diagnostic reference. Host-owned run diagnostics must not depend on the failed connector.

## Related independent reports (not evidence from our account)

- [openai/codex#48940](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/48940) — GitHub scheduled write safety refusal; comments include controlled interactive comparisons.
- [openai/codex#38350](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/38350) — recurring Work tasks become Paused without authorization; a *separate* scheduler-lifecycle problem we have also encountered historically.
- [openai/codex#50769](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/50769) — authorization-context confusion with Dots/GitHub; related but not an identical surface.
- [openai/codex#52714](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/52714) — size-dependent GitHub approval despite Allow all actions in a separate controlled test; **our report does not establish that payload size caused our failures**.
- [OpenAI community: cross-provider scheduled safety checks](https://community.openai.com/t/regression-scheduled-tasks-safety-checks-block-authorized-gmail-sends-and-google-sheets-writes/1403242) — independent Gmail/Google Sheets/Trello/GitHub reports, including successful interactive Trello controls.
- [EndlessZen owner-side investigation #260](https://github.com/drevendev/EndlessZen/issues/260) — dated evidence, incident references, local counterexamples, diagnostic taxonomy and mitigations.

### Public incident context, not a single universal diagnosis

OpenAI acknowledged separate incidents during the period, including [Sep 29: tasks could fail to start/resume/finish during a settings-connection exhaustion incident](https://status.openai.com/incidents/01M3Q4RK1SM4EMK445GGPG7C0N/write-up), [Oct 5–6: Work Mode issue affecting scheduled tasks](https://status.openai.com/incidents/01M45E0JFFJZ6EQ3BWYPW74R2Z), and [Oct 9: apps/plugins availability incident](https://status.openai.com/incidents/01M4HA7BCCXVHTR5DCYMSBQF2H). These were individually bounded incidents; **we do not claim they establish a continuous weeks-long outage or explain every failed run**.

## Requested action

1. Confirm which execution-policy, approval and connector-runtime differences exist between **unattended Scheduled** and **manually initiated** ChatGPT Work runs, especially when both are configured with app-level Allow all actions.
2. Investigate false-positive pre-provider GitHub safety blocks and silent/ambiguous app writes; correlate with host traces rather than requiring user-generated logs through the failed path.
3. Provide host-owned redacted run/error diagnostics and an explicit approval/remediation path when user-granted app permission is insufficient.
4. Distinguish actual provider HTTP failures from host policy refusals, missing file-handoff capabilities, corrupt-success document writes, and local agent bookkeeping deadlocks.
5. Route the report to the right **ChatGPT Work/Scheduled/connector** owning team if this is not maintained by the open-source Codex CLI team.

Sanitized public report. No private repository names, credentials, task identifiers, internal document IDs or payloads are included.

items.title: [Feature Request] Native VBA macro support — editing, execution, and Excel compatibility
items.body:
## Summary

I would like to propose adding native VBA (Visual Basic for Applications) support to GridCraft, including the ability to **create, edit, save, and execute VBA macros**, with compatibility with existing Microsoft Excel `.xlsm` workbooks as the long-term goal.

I understand that implementing a fully compatible VBA environment would be a substantial undertaking, especially for a cross-platform application written in Rust. However, I believe this could become one of GridCraft's most valuable features, particularly for users who want to migrate away from Microsoft Excel without losing their existing automation workflows.

Related discussions:
- #6 — VBA Macros support
- #356 — Possibility of Macros

## Motivation

VBA remains widely used in professional Excel workflows, including financial models, reporting, data processing, document generation, and internal business tools.

For many users, the primary obstacle to replacing Excel is not spreadsheet functionality itself, but the inability to execute existing macros.

GridCraft already provides:
- A spreadsheet engine written in Rust.
- A command-based architecture.
- Built-in automation, scripting, CLI, and MCP interfaces.
- `.xlsm` support with VBA project preservation.

These capabilities could provide a useful foundation for integrating a VBA runtime.

The goal would not simply be to introduce another scripting language, but to eventually allow existing Excel VBA macros to run in GridCraft without requiring users to rewrite them.

## Proposed functionality

### 1. VBA macro execution

Allow users to execute VBA procedures from existing `.xlsm` workbooks.

For example:

```vb
Sub Example()
    Worksheets("Sheet1").Range("A1").Value = 42
    Worksheets("Sheet1").Range("A2").Value = "Hello from VBA"
End Sub
```

Ideally, basic macros like this would work without modification.

Long-term compatibility should include common VBA language constructs, standard library functions, and the Excel object model (`Application`, `Workbook`, `Worksheet`, `Range`, `Cells`, etc.).

### 2. VBA editor

Provide an integrated editor for creating and modifying VBA macros.

Desirable functionality includes:

- Creating, editing, and deleting modules and procedures.
- Syntax highlighting and basic error reporting.
- Running procedures directly from the editor.
- Managing VBA projects embedded in workbooks.
- Optional autocompletion and LSP integration.
- Debugging support (breakpoints, stepping, variable inspection) in later development stages.

Full replication of the Visual Basic Editor would not be necessary initially.

### 3. Excel file compatibility

Support both importing existing VBA projects and saving newly created or modified VBA code into Excel-compatible `.xlsm` files.

The ideal workflow would be:

1. Open an existing `.xlsm` workbook.
2. Inspect and edit its VBA modules.
3. Execute supported macros within GridCraft.
4. Save the workbook.
5. Open the saved workbook in Microsoft Excel with the VBA project still functional.

I understand that modifying and rebuilding `vbaProject.bin` is significantly more complicated than simply preserving its original bytes.

### 4. Events and UI integration

Eventually, support common Excel VBA events such as:

- `Workbook_Open`
- `Worksheet_Change`
- `Worksheet_SelectionChange`

Existing macro-enabled workbook UI elements, such as buttons assigned to macros, could also be supported.

UserForms and more advanced Office integration could remain long-term goals.

## Possible implementation approaches

I am not proposing a specific mandatory implementation. A few possible approaches worth evaluating are:

### Option A — Native VBA interpreter in Rust

Implement or integrate a VBA parser and interpreter that maps supported VBA operations to GridCraft's internal spreadsheet engine.

A possible architecture:

```text
VBA source / imported VBA project
             |
             v
       VBA parser / AST
             |
             v
       VBA interpreter
             |
             v
    Excel Object Model adapter
             |
             v
       GridCraft engine
```

**Advantages:**
- Native cross-platform integration.
- No dependency on Microsoft Office or Wine.
- Direct access to GridCraft's existing engine.
- Greater control over security and compatibility.

**Challenges:**
- VBA language semantics, including Variants, ByRef arguments, default properties, error handling, and COM-related behavior.
- Implementing a compatible subset of the Excel object model.
- Reading, editing, and writing VBA projects.

### Option B — Integrate an existing VBA-compatible runtime

Investigate existing open-source VBA or Visual Basic interpreters and evaluate whether one could be integrated into GridCraft through a Rust interface.

This could avoid implementing the entire language runtime from scratch.

However, compatibility, licensing, maintenance, portability, and integration complexity would need to be carefully evaluated.

### Option C — VBA-to-intermediate-language transpilation

Parse VBA into an AST or intermediate representation and translate supported constructs into another language/runtime, such as JavaScript.

GridCraft's existing command API could serve as the bridge to spreadsheet operations.

This might provide a faster path to an initial implementation, although differences in runtime semantics could make high compatibility difficult.

### Option D — External compatibility backend

As an optional transitional solution, investigate executing macros through an external compatibility layer, potentially using LibreOffice or another existing office runtime.

This would not provide truly native VBA support, and compatibility with Excel VBA would still be limited. However, it might be useful as an experimental fallback.

## Suggested development roadmap

Rather than attempting full VBA compatibility immediately, implementation could be divided into milestones.

**Phase 1 — Basic execution**
- Extract and parse VBA source from existing `.xlsm` files.
- Execute simple procedures with variables, conditions, loops, and function calls.
- Support basic operations on cells, ranges, and worksheets.
- Allow manual execution of macros.

**Phase 2 — Editing and saving**
- Add a basic VBA code editor.
- Support creating and modifying modules.
- Save VBA projects into valid `.xlsm` files.
- Verify interoperability with Microsoft Excel.

**Phase 3 — Expanded compatibility**
- Implement additional VBA language features and built-in functions.
- Expand the Excel object model.
- Support workbook and worksheet events.
- Improve error handling and compatibility testing.

**Phase 4 — Advanced functionality**
- Debugging tools.
- UserForms.
- Additional Excel automation interfaces.
- Further compatibility with real-world macro-enabled workbooks.

Full Windows COM/ActiveX compatibility could remain outside the initial scope, especially on non-Windows platforms.

## Security considerations

Because VBA macros can perform potentially dangerous operations, security should be considered from the beginning.

I would suggest:

- Never automatically execute macros from untrusted documents.
- Require explicit user consent before enabling execution.
- Provide a clear distinction between trusted and untrusted workbooks.
- Investigate sandboxing, permission restrictions, or process isolation.
- Warn users about unsupported operations and compatibility limitations.

Cross-platform support should not require unrestricted access to the host operating system.

## Acceptance criteria for an initial implementation

A useful first milestone could be considered complete when a user can:

- Open a macro-enabled Excel workbook.
- View its existing VBA procedures.
- Execute a simple VBA macro that reads and modifies cells.
- Create or modify a basic VBA procedure.
- Save the result as `.xlsm`.
- Reopen the file in Excel and execute the saved supported VBA procedure.

This would already provide meaningful functionality without requiring complete VBA compatibility.

## Final thoughts

I understand that the project currently considers VBA execution outside its scope.

However, I believe **VBA compatibility could be a major differentiator for GridCraft**, especially for Linux users and organizations trying to reduce their dependence on proprietary office software.

It could also complement GridCraft's existing scripting, CLI, and MCP architecture rather than replace it.

Thank you for considering this proposal!

items.title: P0 — GPT-First Materials Sync: eliminate Antigravity handoff using existing GAS pipeline
items.body:
## Objective (27 Oct 2026)
Enable ChatGPT **GPT-first** completion of owner-authorized Materials/Procurement updates end-to-end without an Antigravity handoff. Preserve Excel Master Drive ID/formulas/formatting, use the **existing** GAS -> /api/sync/drive -> `drive_sync_replace_materials_tools` pipeline, prove Source→DB→authenticated UI parity, and keep production access controls.

## Verified current facts
- Canonical Materials Master ID: `1Yr9iNVo54g4PrB2ntFb6E_ouI_ohHqSn`; changed at 2026-10-27 07:32:09Z. Related PLs `PL0000977 / PC691022001` and `PL0000980 / PC691023001` are in Master.
- Last directly verified materials sync audit 2026-10-27 07:19:29Z: `source unchanged, sync skipped`, rows_read=0, rows_written=0 — **this predates the source edit and alone does not diagnose a bug**. Require post-edit log before deciding whether source-change detector fails.
- Existing GAS scheduler repo snapshot `docs/apps-script/ShiftSyncScheduler_2026-10-13.gs` schedules Materials at Bangkok 08/11/14/17, calling `shiftMaterials20261013_` with `force:false`. Repo snapshots may not match live GAS. Live GAS project ID known, but current ChatGPT Google Drive plugin lacks Apps Script execution/project scopes.
- Existing API `app/api/sync/drive/route.ts` accepts authenticated `x-sync-key` and XLSX body, dispatches existing Materials parser/RPC. **Do not put sync key or Supabase service key in chat/GitHub.**
- This ChatGPT session's linked Supabase **management** connector can read `procurement_items` and `drive_sync_runs` without changing Production RLS. An Antigravity anonymous-key 42501 is not a reason to relax RLS. Authenticated website readback still requires an owner session / approved runner.
- Live GAS metadata was modified at 2026-10-27 07:44Z during current work; avoid parallel edits until existing Antigravity round is complete.

## P0 acceptance / repair plan
1. **Diagnose before changes**: compare post-14:32 source revision with the first subsequent scheduled GAS import and DB log; verify installed time-based triggers and actual live `syncMaterialsWorkbook_` change gating. Distinguish intentional skip from failed detection. Check for duplicate/missing target rows by (source_sheet, source_row) and PC/PL identity; avoid full table resets.
2. **GPT-trigger bridge (one-time activation, only if timing/permissions require)**: prefer a narrow owner-only **Google Sheets request register** writable with the already connected Google Drive/Sheets tools and read by the existing GAS account. Each row only allows the fixed `materials` action + canonical Drive Master File ID + source revision + opaque request ID. Integrate with existing GAS scheduled handler if practical; add a minimal low-frequency polling trigger only if necessary and quota-reviewed. GAS invokes the EXISTING `shiftMaterials20261013_()` path; does not implement a new parser, importer, Supabase writer, or API bypass. Strict source freshness, fixed-file allowlist, idempotency, LockService, replay/duplicate guard, state `REQUESTED/RUNNING/WAIT_SYNC/COMPLETE/ERROR`, bounded retries, no arbitrary code execution or user-supplied URLs. If Google Sheets scope isn't already approved, request exact scope authorization once (never silently broaden).
3. **Verification**: GPT reads exact Source cells / revision via Drive connector, `drive_sync_runs` and `procurement_items` via existing Supabase connector; authenticated /materials and /procurement owner UI readback using an approved agent browser session. Mark completion **only** with matching source+DB+UI evidence; 0 writes or a 200 response is not PASS. Keep receipt unverified absent evidence.
4. **Security & gates**: no service_role in browser/ChatGPT/GitHub; no bypass of SSO, RLS, permissions, or credential exposure; restrict queue to owner+GAS and one approved action; reject unrecognized source IDs, altered permissions and expired requests; rollback queue runner independently. No edits to Defect, Payroll, Daily Reports, Calendar, or production identity/role matrix.
5. **Release**: reconcile Git GAS snapshot with live content before patch; isolated branch/PR, test on QA sheet/workbook, CI/security review then explicit owner-approved release gate. Verify trigger registered, single request exactly one import, idempotent repeat, failure retry, unauthorized attempt denied, and UI source parity. Do not mark DONE on a code-only PR or dry run.
6. **SOP**: retain ACTIVE SOP 06 and SOP 13, which already require existing sync and readback. If bridge is activated, append only the canonical owner-authorized `GPT_FIRST_MATERIALS_SYNC_REQUEST` subflow as an ACTIVE revision after live QA. Do not edit SOP Index until that acceptance.

## Current status
DESIGN / INVESTIGATION. No deployment, new privileges, DB change or live GAS update is included in this issue. Do not race the concurrent Antigravity sync closure. Goal: after one-time controlled integration, future ChatGPT prompts can request sync and verify end-to-end without handoff.

items.title: Arete GoDaddy website → Azure: source/data preservation, staging and cutover
items.body:
## Objective and scope

**OWNER-CONFIRMED PRODUCTION FACT (2026-10-24):** The GoDaddy-built website is **still** Arete Advisory Group's operating website at `areteadvisorygroup.com`. This supersedes earlier migration notes incorrectly treating ChatGPT Sites as the website's authoritative production source. Use the **existing GoDaddy site** as the primary content/functionality baseline and the appropriate GoDaddy product backup/export path as the main migration workstream. Verify its exact product configuration, DNS origin, and data stores with authenticated account evidence; such technical details have not yet been independently certified. Do not substitute an unverified HTML copy or disrupt inquiries, survey records, the domain, or GoDaddy email.

**Do not conflate the production GoDaddy website with CROWN SaaS, Jireh staging, or a separately catalogued ChatGPT Site project.** Preserve GoDaddy publishing and any historically distinct Site content until reviewed. A ChatGPT Site source export is **not** a prerequisite unless actual Arete production features or uniquely retained content/data are proved to depend on it.

## Source-of-truth verification correction (2026-10-24)

**OWNER-CONFIRMED:** The GoDaddy-built website remains the owner's operating Arete website. Do not dispute the owner's operational identification or treat a separate ChatGPT Sites project as the sole migration source.

**HOSTING TECHNICAL ATTRIBUTION — NOT VERIFIED:** Earlier August 26–September 1, 2026 screenshot-based project notes reported GoDaddy-managed domain DNS configured with an OpenAI Site verification record and web routing values associated with ChatGPT Sites, including a `www` CNAME targeting `custom-domains.chatgpt.site`. These are **historical, secondhand records**, not current authoritative DNS or HTTP headers. They may reflect a GoDaddy-built site, a redesigned Site served on a GoDaddy-managed domain, or different versions of the website. They do **not** override the owner's account-level knowledge. Establish the actual current combination via GoDaddy **My Products**, current domain-zone settings, and a live network header/DNS inspection before choosing the export/cutover mechanism. Do not assume registrar = website origin.

**MIGRATION KIT v6 DOCUMENTATION SUPERSEDED:** Its README, SOURCE_AND_AZURE_ACCESS.md, and RELEASE_GATES.md continue to assert that ChatGPT Sites is the only authoritative source and instruct against the GoDaddy builder. Those instructions are **incorrect for the owner-confirmed migration scope**. The independently repeated 41/41 Python offline unit tests and ZIP integrity verify the local audit code only, not platform attribution or readiness. **Do not follow v6's source/export/runbook instructions until corrected.** No new release package or PR was created for this correction.

**LIVE PAGE AND DATA EVIDENCE:** Public website content and contact/survey/assessment interfaces are observable; HTTP response headers, current origin server, active GoDaddy product SKU, publication setting, complete DNS zone, backed data stores, actual form POST handling and delivery have **not** been independently verified. An October 14, 2026 original emailed website report said the private Site tables contained 1 survey row (dated October 11), 1 inquiry row marked as test, and 1,097 analytics rows at that historical time. **Not current counts or proof of GoDaddy storage.** Connected research workbook read on October 24 shows zero rows in `Live Responses` and `Controlled Intake`; it is not a production database backup.

**Release gate remains blocked:** No site source/data export or Azure staging cutover until the current GoDaddy product plus historical/possible separate ChatGPT Site dependencies are reconciled with actual evidence; do not erase either system. Keep GoDaddy email and website DNS unchanged.

## Verified October 24, 2026 Azure evidence reconciliation

- **Authenticated evidence, already collected:** [Run #40011310836](https://github.com/Arete0920/Crown-CSMS/actions/runs/40011310836) (event `workflow_dispatch`, Git SHA `9e846d58275fc51fec0e545394f19306f244f89f`), completed 2026-10-23 19:27 UTC. The `azure-inventory` job used existing federated login successfully; no need to rerun merely to prove access.
- **Scoped inventory only:** 27 resources in `crown-rg`, including two Free-tier Azure Static Web Apps named `crown-dash` and `jireh-site`. **No Arete consulting website resource identified in that resource group.** Do not infer that other resource groups/subscriptions are empty or that CROWN/Jireh sites can be repurposed.
- **Separate runtime truth:** CROWN's production API returned HTTP 200 and database `ok` in the 2026-10-23 inventory, but the release collector still reports `NOT VERIFIED`. Neither result certifies Arete.
- **Costs/budgets unresolved:** the Jireh collector reported zero resource-group budgets; independent redacted cost diagnostics include `AUTHENTICATION`/request failures for some periods and budget reads. Spending cannot be approved from these records; confirm costs/alerts before provisioning.
- **Artifacts verified and downloaded for review (expire 2026-10-30):** runtime inventory `12527270038` ZIP SHA-256 `71d6da64ee395c2f1c067d70e888378eb527f9ffbcd10f484e476fe7d18b752d`; Jireh site `12527230184` SHA-256 `29a90d57583cebf39585b1ca52f61182401b35dcc403291f763046ec77906438`; cost diagnostics `12527135533` SHA-256 `9706b08fefedb3103de4adf155325fb8b3cb056e31819bb989da5dfe38561fc1`; resource inventory `12525913150` SHA-256 `33db21bc5a9d773403e13a03ffa2f8636bc2bd3c9212ca7ad4c930ea52b92e06`. These artifact ZIPs contain operational details and must remain private; only the sanitized summary belongs in this public issue.
- **Owner-confirmed correction (2026-10-24): the GoDaddy-built site remains the operating production website.** Earlier claims that ChatGPT Sites was the only production source were wrong. The separate ChatGPT Site Library projection cannot be materialized, but that is **not** the GoDaddy production website and should not block GoDaddy migration unless verified dependencies emerge. Identify the active GoDaddy product (Websites + Marketing, WordPress, cPanel, or other) and its authenticated backup/export controls. Do not assume a complete native-code export is possible from any proprietary site builder.
- **Revised next proofs:** (1) authenticate the **current GoDaddy website product** and inventory its pages, media, forms, appointments and storage; independently inspect DNS and origin settings for technical migration planning without disputing the owner's confirmed platform; (2) preserve/export GoDaddy content and all other real data sources; (3) confirm Azure resource/cost permissions; (4) build and test an isolated Azure staging site; (5) reversible DNS cutover only after owner acceptance. No Work units or production DNS/email changes used during this checkpoint.

## Verified state (2026-10-24)

- **Separate ChatGPT Site record (NOT the owner-confirmed operating website):** `arete-advisory-group`, project ID `appgprj_6a8f1e50c2e08191b52bac1a41c5718b`; Library metadata reports active/public, source version 80, projection revision 106. This metadata is not evidence that the site replaces the **still-operating GoDaddy website** and must not drive primary migration priorities.
- Public domain `https://areteadvisorygroup.com/` is accessible, including `/contact`, `/survey/technology`, `/assessments/school-health-pulse`, `/solomon`, `/solutions`, and `/privacy`. Independent form submissions / database behavior were **not** tested; do not mark them operationally certified.
- **GoDaddy site and domain configuration need direct inspection:** preserve the current registrar, DNS hosting, MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC and other mail-related records without assuming the registrar, authoritative nameservers and website origin are the same service.
- CROWN repository already contains a read-only GitHub Actions Azure inventory: `.github/workflows/azure-classroom-preflight.yml` with a manual `workflow_dispatch` (including Azure federated auth). Reuse it; do not create duplicate Azure inventory scripts or loosen protection.
- Jireh's **separate** Free-SKU Azure Static Web App staging is reported verified in issue #182, deployment run `39163035972`; **not** proof of Arete migration.
- The connected Site Library file is a **text projection**, not deployable source; materialization explicitly returns `files.materialize is unavailable for Site projections`. No Site-export or Azure Resource Manager write action is exposed by available connectors. No Arete source archive, deployment, DNS change or production cutover has been performed.
- Public site shows inconsistent legacy navigation/contact information on some older pages (e.g. `/privacy` vs homepage); preserve current content authority and resolve before parity acceptance.

## Priority order and acceptance criteria

### P0: GoDaddy production product inspection, export and data lineage — **BLOCKED, authenticated GoDaddy website administration needed**
- [ ] Inspect **GoDaddy My Products** for the **current, owner-confirmed production website** and identify its precise product (Websites + Marketing vs WordPress/cPanel vs other), domain association, publication status, pages, images, forms, appointments, and supported backup/export tools. This product identification is technical inventory, not a question of whether the GoDaddy site is still in use.
- [ ] Record the current `areteadvisorygroup.com` and `www` DNS, TLS, redirection, and hosting configuration from authenticated GoDaddy settings and a public DNS read. Independently check whether another platform serves any subordinate functionality, but **do not reclassify the production website as ChatGPT Sites based on the existence of a separate Sites project.** Keep complete DNS/email records private.
- [ ] Collect original GoDaddy-built site content/assets and appropriate backups **separately** from any distinct ChatGPT Site source/database/file storage. If GoDaddy is Websites + Marketing, its Site History backup covers sections/text/settings, **not** blog/email/product/appointment/image data; those require separate inventories (official GoDaddy help: https://www.godaddy.com/en-ca/help/back-up-my-website-32228). If WordPress/cPanel, apply the corresponding native file/database export process.
- [ ] **Conditional only:** if independent evidence proves that a distinct ChatGPT Site supplies production endpoints, unique content, or retained data, preserve that specific component and assess supported source/storage export. **Do not block the GoDaddy website migration solely on an unrelated ChatGPT Sites export.**
- [ ] Determine whether the Site uses D1 relational storage, R2 file storage, or other persistence and identify **owned** data exports, retention, consent and rollback requirements. Do not fabricate empty data/missing records.
- [ ] Map every browser-facing write endpoint, email routing, appointment confirmation, research submission, and persisted response to a production-equivalent Azure service. Confirm record counts and integrity using private evidence.
- [ ] Reconcile live site with the current Arete Website & Brand Content Authority and Website Production Change Register in Google Drive before migrating out-of-date pages.

### P0: Existing Azure resource and cost proof — **PENDING authenticated run**
- [x] **Reuse completed Azure inventory run**, rather than dispatching again: [Azure Classroom Release Preflight #40011310836](https://github.com/Arete0920/Crown-CSMS/actions/runs/40011310836), completed successfully October 23, 2026, on `main` commit `9e846d58275fc51fec0e545394f19306f244f89f`. Federated Azure login and read-only inventory job both succeeded. See checkpoint below. Do not paste raw artifacts or secrets into issue.
- [ ] Confirm subscription, tenant, resource group, Azure role permissions, Static Web Apps capacity and existing app ownership, staging DNS/TLS, and incremental cost/alerts. Reuse verified Azure infrastructure only when safe.
- [ ] Do not provision paid resources without explicit cost authorization.

### P1: Private staging
- [ ] Restore compatible source to a separately isolated, non-indexed Azure staging hostname; lock administrative access; use test data or a separately authorized sanitized migration; no production record mutation.
- [ ] Prove exact deployed build/source identity, HTTP 200 + SPA/deep-link behavior, canonical and sitemap correctness, accessibility and mobile browser parity, assets, security headers and redirects.
- [ ] End-to-end consented test of `/contact` intake, verification/acknowledgment, appropriate mailbox/CRM/calendar routing, duplicate/retry behavior, abuse guards, audit visibility, and no data loss.
- [ ] End-to-end consented test of `/survey/technology` persistence, aggregate privacy, optional follow-up isolation, and reconciliation with existing data.
- [ ] Verify all browser-only assessment and knowledge tools remain client-only unless specifically designed otherwise.
- [ ] Confirm privacy, terms, cookie/storage behavior, and outbound/inbound service allowlists.

### P1: DNS cutover, rollback and close
- [ ] Take a private, timestamped DNS baseline, including A/AAAA/CNAME/CAA/TXT/MX plus SPF/DKIM/DMARC and any verification records.
- [ ] Only alter website records after Azure staging and owner acceptance are green; keep GoDaddy domain registration and all mail-related records unchanged.
- [ ] Validate apex and `www`, HTTPS certificate/renewal, canonical SEO and one-to-one redirects, actual inquiry delivery, survey integrity, client app behavior, and active monitoring.
- [ ] Set a timed rollback decision/owner and retain original DNS values plus Site rollback path; ensure no writes disappear in a split-traffic window.
- [ ] Attach sanitized Azure deployment ID, source commit/hash, verification timestamp, test outcomes and rollback proof. Close only after production readback, not merely merged code.

## Existing references
- Current public website: https://areteadvisorygroup.com/
- Existing Azure workflow: https://github.com/Arete0920/Crown-CSMS/actions/workflows/azure-classroom-preflight.yml
- Jireh separate proof (do not reuse as Arete acceptance): https://github.com/Arete0920/Crown-CSMS/issues/182
- Sites owner UI: https://chatgpt.com/sites
- **Operating source determined by owner:** GoDaddy-built website **still active and in use**. The ChatGPT Sites record is a separate resource, not the primary migration source. The exact GoDaddy product, source portability and data inventory remain to be authenticated; avoid duplicating projects.

## Change policy
No new repository, paid resource, DNS edits, email routing changes, secret publication, unreviewed data migration, or production claims without evidence. Keep CROWN's protected branch, limited change scope, and exact-head checks intact. This is an operational tracker; opening it does not approve production changes.

items.title: Migrate operational data state from Google Sheets to PostgreSQL
items.body:
## Approved architecture

Use PostgreSQL as the operational source of truth, retain Google Sheets as the operator/decision interface, and add BigQuery only after the operational path is stable for append-only analytical history.

The binding implementation plan and initial additive schema are in draft PR #23.

## Safety invariant

`runtime_enabled=false` remains unchanged. No recommendation, scoring, trading, or destructive workbook behavior is activated by this migration.

## Phase tracker

### Phase 0 — evidence and freshness contract
- [ ] Rotate the exposed EODHD token and update secrets without posting its value.
- [ ] Create and verify an immutable pre-migration workbook backup.
- [ ] Extend `PAGE-VERDICT` with requested/fresh/preserved/coverage/stubs/identity/provider/API evidence.
- [ ] Make artifact audit fail when freshness is inadequate even if rows were written.

### Phase 1 — PostgreSQL foundation
- [x] Draft additive operational schema in PR #23.
- [x] Draft non-destructive schema contract test in PR #23.
- [ ] Add repository interface behind a disabled shadow flag.
- [ ] Add migration runner and environment validation without provisioning production automatically.

### Phase 2 — shadow dual-write
- [ ] Persist successful batches to PostgreSQL while Sheets remains canonical.
- [ ] Reconcile row counts and hashes for three consecutive complete cycles.
- [ ] Record differences without changing recommendations.

### Phase 3 — incremental refresh and API budget
- [ ] Add TTL by data class.
- [ ] Add shared weighted EODHD usage ledger and reserve thresholds.
- [ ] Prevent repeated fetches of still-fresh data.

### Phase 4 — worker-first orchestration
- [ ] Confirm Render Postgres, Key Value, and worker runtime settings.
- [ ] Move long-running provider work out of the web request path.
- [ ] Start with one active page worker; test max two only with load evidence.

### Phase 5 — operational cutover
- [ ] Publish Sheets from one validated PostgreSQL snapshot.
- [ ] Prove the decision surfaces can be rebuilt without provider calls.
- [ ] Keep operator-owned cells and rollback path.

### Phase 6 — BigQuery analytics
- [ ] Export append-only snapshot and recommendation history.
- [ ] Reconcile no-action and cost-adjusted performance outcomes.

## Acceptance gates

- portfolio and decision-candidate critical fields: 100% fresh;
- market universes: at least 95% fresh;
- published identity failures: zero;
- unknown critical values remain explicit `UNKNOWN`;
- three consecutive scheduled cycles pass;
- Sheets are reproducible from a database snapshot;
- explicit owner approval is recorded before any runtime activation.

Refs #18 and #23.
